environment.description: Same Laravel application deployed on EC2 behind AWS ALB with an associated AWS WAFv2 Web ACL. The Web ACL includes the AWS managed rule group `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` (priority 1) with `CrossSiteScripting_BODY`, `CrossSiteScripting_QUERYARGUMENTS`, `CrossSiteScripting_COOKIE`, and `CrossSiteScripting_URIPATH` rules all in default action (BLOCK). Additionally, the managed rule group `AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet` (priority 2) is attached with all rules in BLOCK mode. The Web ACL default action is ALLOW. CloudWatch metrics confirm both rule groups are actively evaluating traffic with non-zero BlockedRequests counts. The WAF is associated at the ALB level via `aws wafv2 associate-web-acl`. Note: the application itself still contains the vulnerability — the WAF operates as a transparent inline filter on all HTTP request parameters before they reach the application layer.
